events.title: Trump–Xi Washington summit
events.why_it_matters: Highest-stakes US–China event of the quarter: ~$30bn tariff-cut talk, rare earths, AI guardrails, Taiwan arms, and the Nov 10 Busan truce expiry, with US midterms six weeks out.
events.what_to_watch: Whether leaders extend the trade truce, cut non-sensitive tariffs, lock an AI-incident notification channel, or put the ~$14bn Taiwan arms package on the table.

events.title: Hormuz tanker war still live; Brent ~$101–103
events.why_it_matters: Visible Hormuz transits remain a trickle versus ~125/day pre-war after the Sept 17–18 IRGC strike on Togo-flagged tanker Trend; the $100 oil print is a war premium, not a demand story, and it is feeding the Warsh Fed's hike path.
events.what_to_watch: UNGA Iran remarks, any US–Iran side channel, IRGC 'sanctions zone' expansion, and whether escorted Saudi/Iraq barrels keep Brent from re-spiking above $110.

events.title: UNGA 81 high-level debate; Trump speaks Sept 22
events.why_it_matters: Trump speaks the morning of Sept 22 (after Brazil) with Pezeshkian on Sept 23; Hormuz, Iran nuclear, China, and Ukraine lines can move oil, defense, and tariff-sensitive names into the Xi visit.
events.what_to_watch: Any 'deal, squeeze, or destroy' language on Iran, a possible Pezeshkian sideline, and whether Trump ties Hormuz reopening to sanctions relief.

events.title: Trump–Zelensky UNGA sideline; energy-truce push
events.why_it_matters: After a Sept 20 call, the two agreed to meet in New York to test a reciprocal halt on energy-infrastructure strikes that have lifted global diesel; Trump just signed the Graham Russia/Iran sanctions law.
events.what_to_watch: Whether an energy/Black Sea ceasefire is announced, and if Kyiv suspends Russian-refinery strikes in exchange for a real Russian pause.

events.title: Bessent–He Lifeng pre-summit talks (New York)
events.why_it_matters: Eight-hour Treasury–Vice Premier session at JPMorgan HQ was called 'very successful' and teed up a US–China AI dialogue plus tariff/rare-earth working groups for Sept 24.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the AI notification mechanism and non-sensitive tariff cuts survive the leaders' meeting, or get watered down over Taiwan/Iran finance.

events.title: Warsh Fed 25bp hike to 3.75–4.00% with hawkish SEP
events.why_it_matters: First Warsh hike, 12-0, with a majority of dots implying at least one more 25bp by year-end as gasoline/Hormuz inflation stays sticky; 10y yields have printed above 5%.
events.what_to_watch: Sept 22–23 Fed speakers (Jefferson, Barr), Aug PCE on Sept 30, and Oct 2 NFP as inputs to the Oct 27–28 FOMC; no decision in this window.

events.title: BoJ hikes 25bp to 1.25% (31-year high)
events.why_it_matters: 7-2 hike to 1.25% one session after the Warsh Fed completes G3 tightening and is the classic yen-carry unwind trigger with oil imports already stressing Japan's trade balance; policy rate effective Sept 24.
events.what_to_watch: USD/JPY and global credit/FX vol as the hike settles, plus Typhoon Dujuan disruption to Kanto activity this week.

events.title: ECB hikes 25bp; deposit rate 2.50%
events.why_it_matters: Second 2026 hike, driven by Middle East energy inflation; staff see 2026 HICP at 3.0% and markets price ~75% odds of another 25bp on Oct 28–29.
events.what_to_watch: Whether Hormuz keeps euro-area energy sticky enough to lock in the October hike.

events.title: BoE holds Bank Rate at 3.75% (6–3 hawkish hold)
events.why_it_matters: MPC held 6–3 with three members wanting +25bp as CPI 3.1% is seen heading toward 4% in early 2027 on energy; QT gilt sales paused six months.
events.what_to_watch: Next decision is Nov 5, outside this window; UK rates now a lagging G3 story unless oil spikes again.

events.title: PBOC holds LPR 16th month (3.00%/3.50%)
events.why_it_matters: Unanimous hold confirms Beijing will not offset G3 hikes with a big easing even as FAI and consumption wilt into the Trump–Xi meeting.
events.what_to_watch: Any post-summit credit/property package; next LPR is mid-October, outside this window.

events.title: China August activity: IP +5.2%, retail +0.4%, FAI −7.2%
events.why_it_matters: Export/high-tech supply is still running (high-tech IP +16.7%) while domestic demand and property (dev. investment −19.9% YTD) are in a deepening slump — the imbalance Xi brings to Washington.
events.what_to_watch: Whether summit optics produce a consumption/property support signal; September NBS prints are mid-October.

events.title: Graham Russia/Iran Act signed (secondary-tariff authority)
events.why_it_matters: H.R. 5334 is now law: expands Russia/Iran sanctions and authorizes up to 100% secondary tariffs on top purchasers of Russian oil/gas (China/India) plus up to 500% duties on Russian goods — a live tariff gun next to the Xi summit.
events.what_to_watch: How fast Trump uses waiver vs. secondary-tariff authority, and whether Beijing treats it as a summit poison pill.

events.title: US Section 338 import bans on selected Canadian goods
events.why_it_matters: Sept 8 proclamations escalate the Canada tit-for-tat from 50% tariffs (scope modified Sept 15) to outright bans on specified beer/wine/spirits, some dairy/whey, and motorcycles at 12:01 a.m. ET Sept 29.
events.what_to_watch: CBP annex lists, Canadian retaliation, and any last-minute carve-outs before the ban date.

events.title: Google ad-tech remedies (no breakup)
events.why_it_matters: Judge Brinkema rejected a DOJ AdX breakup (Sept 2) and on Sept 16 imposed six-year behavioral remedies plus a compliance monitor — another Big Tech case that stopped short of structural relief.
events.what_to_watch: DOJ appeal decision and how open-bidding/data-sharing rules hit GOOGL ad-tech take rate.

events.title: SEC 5-year 'innovation exemption' for tokenized NMS stocks
events.why_it_matters: Temporary exemptive order lets permissioned on-chain venues trade tokenized NMS stocks via AMMs — the most concrete US market-structure opening for tokenization this year.
events.what_to_watch: Issuer opt-outs, volume caps, and which brokers/venues actually list; comment file will shape durable rules.

events.title: AutoZone Q4 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Best high-frequency read on US consumer trade-down and DIY auto spend into a rate-hike/oil-shock tape; Street ~$54.42 EPS / ~$6.71bn sales.
events.what_to_watch: Same-store sales, mix into needs vs. discretionary, and any guidance cut tied to gasoline/rates.

events.title: General Mills, Cintas, Paychex Q1 prints
events.why_it_matters: GIS (~$0.72 EPS / ~$4.34bn) is the packaged-food inflation/volume tell; CTAS/PAYX (~$1.35 and ~$1.32 EPS) read US employment and small-business demand after the Warsh hike.
events.what_to_watch: GIS volume vs. price, Cintas facility-count/pricing, Paychex worksite-client growth.

events.title: Costco Q4 and Darden Q1 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Same-day consumer stress test as the Xi summit: Costco membership/traffic (~$6.55 EPS / ~$94.9bn sales) vs. Darden casual dining (~$2.05 EPS / ~$3.21bn) as gasoline, rates, and food inflation squeeze real incomes.
events.what_to_watch: Costco traffic vs. ticket and renewal rates; Darden same-store sales and lower-income cohort commentary.

events.title: US August new home sales
events.why_it_matters: Follows Lennar's order/margin miss, 3.98M existing-home sales, and another starts/permits drop; consensus ~610k–620k SAAR after July's 607k collapse.
events.what_to_watch: A sub-600k print would confirm the housing crack is still deepening into higher mortgage rates.

events.title: US August durable goods orders
events.why_it_matters: First CapEx pulse after the Warsh hike; consensus ~−0.5% m/m after July's +1.1%, with core ex-aircraft the tell for equipment demand.
events.what_to_watch: Nondefense capital goods ex-aircraft; a sharp core miss would validate tighter financial conditions.

events.title: JOLTS August job openings
events.why_it_matters: Labor-demand input to the Warsh path; consensus ~7.2M openings vs July 7.271M — still historically firm if it holds.
events.what_to_watch: Openings/unemployed ratio and quits; a sub-7.0M would be the first real cooling signal into NFP.

events.title: August PCE / Q2 GDP third estimate
events.why_it_matters: Fed's preferred inflation gauge into the next hike debate; core PCE consensus ~0.2–0.25% m/m and ~3.3% y/y, with Q2 GDP third estimate around 1.5–2.0% annualized.
events.what_to_watch: Core PCE vs 3.3% y/y; a 0.3%+ m/m would re-price October hike odds higher.

events.title: Micron FY Q4 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Memory/HBM bellwether for the AI-capex cycle the same week as the Xi AI dialogue and into Nike/ISM the next morning.
events.what_to_watch: HBM supply commentary, data-center mix, and FY27 capex/guidance versus China-export-control risk.

events.title: Nike Q1 FY2027 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Global brand/China-demand tell one week after Trump–Xi; wholesale cleanup and Greater China are the two stock-moving lines.
events.what_to_watch: North America full-price mix, Greater China growth, and inventory/guidance.

events.title: ISM manufacturing PMI (September) + NFP week
events.why_it_matters: Oct 1 ISM (Aug was 54.6 vs 55.2 expected) then Oct 2 NFP; jobs consensus clusters ~140k–160k with unemployment ~4.1% — the last labor print before the Oct 27–28 FOMC.
events.what_to_watch: ISM new orders/prices paid (oil pass-through) and NFP vs ~150k; a hot wages print keeps another Warsh hike alive.

events.title: OPEC+ seven-country meeting (November quotas)
events.why_it_matters: Sept 6 they froze October quotas after unwinding 1.65mbpd of cuts; Hormuz — not paper quotas — is the binding supply constraint, so any November hike would be mostly optics unless the strait reopens.
events.what_to_watch: Hold vs. symbolic cut, and language on Iranian barrels / 2027 capacity baselines.

events.title: Taiwan gray-zone pressure into the summit
events.why_it_matters: Taipei's first multi-type attack-drone joint drill and a mid-September PLA air/naval spike keep semiconductor tail risk in the Sept 24 tape, alongside a pending ~$14bn US arms package Xi wants as a chip.
events.what_to_watch: Any summit language that freezes or delays Taiwan arms, and PLA sortie counts the week of the visit.

events.title: US housing crack still in the data (starts, existing sales, Lennar)
events.why_it_matters: August starts 1.275M (−2.6%), existing sales 3.98M, inventory 4.9 months, and Lennar cut FY deliveries after a Q3 EPS/order miss — housing is already cracking even as nominal retail sales rebounded +1.2%.
events.what_to_watch: Sept 24 new-home sales and builder commentary; mortgage rates after the 10y >5% spike.

events.title: Typhoon Dujuan threatens Tokyo/Kanto (Silver Week)
events.why_it_matters: Powerful storm into Kanto during Silver Week with 300–350mm rain risk, flight/rail cuts, and a possible short hit to Japanese activity just as the BoJ hike becomes effective Sept 24.
events.what_to_watch: Landfall track vs Tokyo, auto/electronics plant downtime, and any yen safe-haven bid.

events.title: Post-FOMC Fed-speak (Jefferson, Barr)
events.why_it_matters: Warsh is not on the circuit this week; Vice Chair Jefferson (Sept 22, Treasury Market Conference) and Gov. Barr (Sept 23, housing) are the first official glosses on the hawkish SEP.
events.what_to_watch: Any pushback on a second 2026 hike, and Barr's read on housing affordability after the starts/sales slump.

events.title: Electra Therapeutics (ETRA) IPO listed
events.why_it_matters: Upsized ~$350M clinical-stage biotech IPO at $15 was the window's risk-appetite test after Holtec pulled its nuclear listing into a hawkish-rate tape; lockup is ~March 2027.
events.what_to_watch: Aftermarket vs biotech beta; no other mega US IPO is on this two-week calendar.

events.title: SEMICON India 2026 (New Delhi)
events.why_it_matters: Modi-opened 600-exhibitor chip gathering (ASML, Applied, Micron, Tata) was the live diversification/CapEx signal while AI demand stays hot; next big show is SEMICON West Oct 13–15 (outside this window).
events.what_to_watch: Follow-through CapEx MOUs; no new market-moving announcement cluster after close.

events.title: FCC clears foreign funding path in Paramount–WBD deal
events.why_it_matters: Media Bureau approved >25% foreign investment in Paramount Skydance's proposed Warner Bros. Discovery acquisition with no-control conditions, unblocking a ~$110bn media combination.
events.what_to_watch: Remaining antitrust/shareholder hurdles; Sept 30 FCC meeting is spectrum/NEPA, not this deal.

top_risks: Hormuz stays functionally closed and Brent re-spikes above $110 into a hawkish Warsh Fed, tightening real incomes and hike odds together.
Trump–Xi fails or trades Taiwan arms / export controls for a thin tariff truce, hitting semis and US allies' security premium.
Graham Act secondary tariffs on China/India oil buyers get brandished during the summit week, collapsing the trade-deal bid.
Housing/consumer confirmation: sub-600k new-home sales plus Costco/Darden/AZO misses into 5% 10-year yields.
BoJ 1.25% + Dujuan + oil-import bill triggers a disorderly yen-carry unwind across global credit.
top_opportunities: A clean Trump–Xi extension of the Nov 10 truce plus non-sensitive tariff cuts and a formal AI dialogue would be the quarter's risk-on catalyst for China-sensitive cyclicals and semis.
UNGA energy/Black Sea truce (Trump–Zelensky) and any Hormuz de-escalation language would crush the oil war premium.
If Aug PCE/NFP cool while retail-sales resilience holds, markets can fade the second-hike SEP dots into October.
Micron HBM/AI guide plus a non-confrontational Xi AI channel would support the semiconductor complex after SEMICON India.
SEC tokenization exemption is a medium-term structural bid for US market-structure/fintech if venues actually launch.
summary: The two-way overlay for the next two weeks is Thursday's Trump–Xi summit (tariff cuts/AI vs Taiwan arms and the newly signed Graham secondary-tariff law) against a still-unresolved Hormuz tanker war with Brent ~$101–103. G3 tightening is done for this window (Warsh 3.75–4.00%, BoJ 1.25% effective Sept 24, ECB 2.50%) so the data that can still reprice the path are Aug PCE (Sept 30) and Oct 2 NFP, while US housing is already cracking even as nominal retail sales rebounded +1.2%.
